source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Age matters more than size when deciding when to mate a gilt (a young female that hasn't yet had piglets). The recommended age to first mate a gilt is about 10 months, when she is roughly 70–80% of her final adult body weight (which itself ranges 60kg to over 100kg depending on breed). Mating a gilt too young or too small will stop her growing and reduce her future litter sizes. Keep the gilt well fed and away from the boar until at least 8–10 months old, then give her daily exposure to a boar for about a month before mating; mating her on her second or third heat (rather than her first) increases the chance of a larger litter. Mate her twice, 12–14 hours apart, on the first day of heat. Gilts that don't conceive after two matings, or that haven't shown heat by 12 months old, should be sold rather than kept for breeding.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
